items.context: Woke with this. No pain, no discharge, vision normal.

img.author: James Heilman, MD (cropped)
img.alt: An eye with a flat, bright red patch covering much of the white, sparing the clear cornea.

items.why: Flat, sharply edged blood under the conjunctiva in a painless eye with normal vision.
items.pearl: Usually from a cough, strain or rub and clears in 1–2 weeks. Check blood pressure, and the INR if they take warfarin.

items.context: A firm lump on the neck that slowly grew after a cut years ago.

img.author: CDC/ Robert S. Craig (cropped)
img.alt: A large, shiny, lobulated dark lump on the side of the neck.

items.why: Firm, rubbery scar tissue that has grown well beyond the original wound.
items.pearl: More common in darker skin. Unlike hypertrophic scars, keloids spread past the wound edge and rarely fade; steroid injections help.

items.context: Itchy lumps after an evening by the river.

img.author: CDC/ Division of Vector-Borne Diseases Rickettsial Zoonoses Branch
img.alt: A forearm with several swollen pink welts merging together.

items.why: Itchy, swollen pink welts on exposed skin that merge together.
items.pearl: Big local reactions are common, especially in children. In Australia, mosquitoes also spread Ross River and Barmah Forest viruses.

items.context: Raised red-purple spots on the legs after a sore throat. Joints ache.

img.author: CDC/ Dr. Charles N. Farmer (cropped)
img.alt: Knees and legs with scattered raised purple spots.

items.why: Palpable purpura on the legs from small-vessel IgA vasculitis.
items.pearl: Mostly in children. Check the urine and blood pressure for weeks afterwards, because kidney involvement can appear late.

items.context: A burning feeling inside both cheeks with spicy food.

img.author: CDC/ Robert E. Sumpter (cropped)
img.alt: Inside of the cheek with a lacy network of fine white lines.

items.why: A lacy white network (Wickham striae) on the inner cheeks, usually on both sides.
items.pearl: Unlike thrush, it doesn't wipe off. It carries a small cancer risk, so long-standing or ulcerated areas need review.

items.context: Fever, sore throat and no cough.

img.author: CDC/ Heinz F. Eichenwald, MD
img.alt: Open mouth showing a red throat with small red spots on the soft palate.

items.why: An angry red throat with petechiae on the soft palate, fever and no cough.
items.pearl: In Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities, treating strep throat with penicillin helps prevent rheumatic fever.

items.context: A gardener with a sore that started after a rose-thorn prick, then new lumps up the arm.

img.author: CDC/ Dr. Lucille K. Georg
img.alt: A forearm with crusted, ulcerated lesions in a line running up from the hand.

items.why: Nodules and ulcers marching up the arm along the lymphatics after a thorn injury.
items.pearl: Known as 'rose gardener's disease'. Itraconazole is the usual treatment, often for months.

items.context: A painful, fast-growing foot ulcer in a man from the Papua New Guinea highlands.

img.author: CDC/ K. Mae Lennon, Tulane Medical School; Clement Benjamin
img.alt: A deep, raw, red ulcer with raised edges on the side of a dark-skinned foot.

items.why: A painful, rapidly enlarging ulcer on the lower leg or foot in a hot, humid climate.
items.pearl: Fusobacteria and spirochaetes are usually involved. Penicillin or metronidazole plus good wound care and nutrition heal most.

items.context: A villager from rural West Africa with a burning blister on the ankle.

img.author: CDC
img.alt: An ankle with a small sore from which a thin white thread is being wound around a matchstick.

items.why: A long thin worm emerging from a painful blister, slowly wound out on a stick.
items.pearl: Close to eradication: fewer than 20 human cases a year recently, down from millions in the 1980s, thanks to filtered drinking water.

items.context: Itchy, patterned rash for years in a man from a remote Pacific island.

img.author: CDC/ Dr. Libero Ajello (cropped)
img.alt: A back and shoulder covered in overlapping concentric rings of fine scale, like wood grain.

items.why: Concentric, overlapping rings of scale like lace or wood grain, from Trichophyton concentricum.
items.pearl: Found in the Pacific islands, South-East Asia and the Amazon, and tends to run in families. It needs oral antifungals.
